decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1.25%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.”

changes.quote: However, the ebbing of geopolitical tensions has rolled back oil prices, bolstered consumer confidence, and strengthened debt and equity markets.

tone_quotes.quote: These developments, along with the accommodative stance of monetary policy and ongoing growth in productivity, should foster an improving economic climate over time.

Although the timing and extent of that improvement remain uncertain, the Committee perceives that over the next few quarters the upside and downside risks to the attainment of sustainable growth are roughly equal.
The Committee believes that, taken together, the balance of risks to achieving its goals is weighted toward weakness over the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.11% APR costs about $54.62 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.84% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.79% would fall by about $15.25 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6%, and employers added an average of -133k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (April 2003); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -10 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates).
